"Nothing is that serious, choose peace." 

I needed this saying more than one could possibly imagine. I'm finally starting to cut news-related content out of my life. It has done nothing but give me mental health anguish. I'm not just talking about being angry or upset, or "Doomscrolling" or even having a "Doomerist mindset". politics, be it from articles I have to read for classes, youtubers, even ones like L.I.M.C that end up bringing up topics related to society, end up triggering suicidal ideation in me. 

I've rarely felt like I "Wanted" to die, not in the emotional sense of the word. But rather, Suicide manifested as a contingency for me. I care a lot about things, about the world, about the people affected by all the bad things that happen, about the idea that society as a whole could collapse, about the United States losing more and more of its principles on human rights to the trump administration, and rather than just making me angry, it makes me drained. Worse, it makes me consider the idea that, if the world itself is going to end, I'm nothing but a liability. News content, for me, bypasses the emotional aspect entirely and reaches a logical conclusion: "if the world is broken, and I am responsible for fixing it (or at least understanding it), and I cannot fix it, then my existence is a liability". So my ideation has never been "I cannot go on, it hurts too much"; it's been "if I can't leave the country in five years, then I'm going to have to kill myself, because I'm going to lose my rights anyway". 

This is why it's become so critical for me to take a step back. I already do way more than most people would in contributing to the things that matter, but my brain has had the idea drilled into it by itself that I needed to help others at the cost of myself, like giving pieces of myself, was the thing I was obligated to do to help make the world at least a little bit better for other people. 

But doing that doesn't help me, and it won't help anyone else substantially enough to avoid diminishing returns. So I need to stop. I already donate $ 45 a month to Food Not Bombs, the Electronic Frontier Foundation, and the Control AI initiative. That's almost $500 annually to non-profits. Despite that, I still sometimes feel like I need to do more, like volunteering or writing more letters to Congress than I already have. 

That's why I need to stop. I really need to stop. I do enough that watching the news doesn't deserve my attention. It never will, and I may need to cut it off entirely, as well as other similar things. They now only ever serve to make my life more painful than it needs to be, to the point that I sometimes forget to even drink water. 

So, in conclusion, thank you for your work; thank you for doing it yourself without AI; thank you for giving me the message I needed to tell myself ever since I first started torturing myself with the false pretense of civil obligation.

Edit: Thank you all for your kind words. To my understanding, this comment was the first written for this video. And I feel like that's brought everyone to take the opportunity to share their own thoughts as well. I've managed to eliminate a ton of the political sources from my life, though it was never the news or anything like it, rather, stuff like YouTube, or newsletters from Control AI Initiative or the EFF. Still, I feel clear for once, even if fleeting. The thing that still makes me prone to negative spirals is the fact that my family has also been dysfunctional. To the guy who went on about "Abusive parents, No. My mom and dad aren't abusive. Saying that doesn't help the situation because it kills nuance. None of the other people in my family is a bad person, but they all have problems. Our dad ghosted my mom, but still wants to "Be part of our life" despite the fact that he doesn't even pay for the house anymore, but even still, he managed to help give me some genuinely good advice that I feel I wouldn't have been able to get through life without. Mom has been struggling as a result of dad's straight up lack of comunication behind what his actual intentions were all of this time, which sometimes leads to her doing things like being dead set on solving problems or goals in one way, and rarely accepting alternatives, which has lead me to struggle to know how to do things independently until only recently, but she still tries all that she can to provide for us even given her current situation. And my sister has been emotionally all over the place due to having been in chronic pain for over three months. She gets into arguments with her mom a lot because she sometimes feels like nobody cares about her. Even so, she genuinely wants to get better, and deeply understands that I'm there to listen to her when she needs it without judgment. she told me specifically she still loves mom, even if she ends up impulsively saying hurtful things from not being able to control her own emotions, and that she herself wishes things would get better so that none of this will have to continue. 

I know this is a whole lot of personal stuff, but I genuinely have absolutely nobody else to talk to about it; the closest I have to a therapist is a speech therapist meant to work with younger kids that we only speak to once a month. He does alright, but our conversations are rarely ever that deep since it's only 30 minutes every month. 

Fortunately, I already have plans for what I will do if things go wrong. My current job has me working dishes at a retirement home for fifteen an hour, while I'm not working a whole lot of time yet, if all else fails, it's a job I'm extremely familliar with after having worked for over a year, I genuinely love the job since it's simple, predictable, I'm great friends with everyone I work with, and we even get free food on our break/to take home from the leftovers so it doesn't get thrown away at the end of the day, as well as health insurance for anyone working full time. While I don't work full-time, the manager is absolutely willing to make any adjustments I've needed to my schedule, provided I communicate with him well in advance. While 30K a year isn't a whole lot, especially with rising prices, My Major life plan is to look into a job in welding. I tried welding once before, and I genuinely loved the process of stick welding. I just signed up for two 5:00 PM to 10:00 PM courses every Monday and Wednesday this fall. They'll probably be long, tiring nights, but it'll be the absolute best way to get into welding initially while still keeping a reasonable schedule, meaning I'll be able to go the rest of the way in the following year once I take on the fully committed 16-hour course. I also plan to get into writing and art as a way to actually bring fulfillment into my life; that is why I also signed up for a drawing and creative writing class this year. 

There will still be a ton of hurdles throughout this plan, most likely, but I'm incredibly young, and having managed to have all of this figured out even before 21 has proven itself to be way bigger of a thing for me than I thought. Especially since I manage to have enough money saved that every single college class I've taken so far has been out of pocket, even if they weren't all that expensive. 

My goal is to get into a state of financial homeostasis; I don't care if that means I'm in an apartment, small home, or wherever. My goal is to get out of the sense of survival, one day at a time. That is what I truly believe will make life worth living, every weld, picture, every word.

People tease, note it as behavior resulting from this this and that, some saying I’ve just always been that way, but none of them are capable of being made aware as to exactly how much I hold back. By whom, we do not know, but we must treat as much time as we can spare, from the bustle of life amidst itself, to make full use of that gift. To use a gift is to thank the sender, as they show their love to you through these conceptual cycles which interminably turn all things. The very universe’s love is shown through our life. Or, perhaps, it could be the universe’s lack of care, according to some. I, personally, am tired of being alone despite all things. I’m so, so tired of being alone. I’m not alone anymore; I now have people who have taken me in with care. This was not always the case. Before moving in, to keep everything vague enough, I lived with my mom, who wasn’t a very good influence on my mental or, ironically, physical health - a fact I’ve managed to accept only recently - and before her was my dad. I had shelter, food, clothes, water, and was being educated as needed, but at what cost? 
I have only recently become human. Only within the past year or two have I been making the developments needed to feed this required data adjustment to make it prove true to my own systems and further demonstrate it to others. With him, I was not human. I was little more than a servant. Furniture. A trophy child trained with impeccable obedience, resistance, skill, patience, and kindness. Really, it’s by whim if not intention of the gods who’d abandoned me for so long that I didn’t get sold off to a worse fate at the hands of one who has violated outside of that which is permissible by any degree. I choose peace for I fear repercussions. I choose peace because I’m tired. I choose peace because, ultimately, I believe it may be out of spite for all those who want me to break. I care a lot about things, about the world, about the people affected by all the bad things that happen, about the idea that society as a whole could collapse, about the United States losing more and more of its principles on human rights to the trump administration, and rather than just making me angry, it makes me drained. Worse, it makes me consider the idea that, if the world itself is going to end, I'm nothing but a liability. News content, for me, bypasses the emotional aspect entirely and reaches a logical conclusion: "if the world is broken, and I am responsible for fixing it (or at least understanding it), and I cannot fix it, then my existence is a liability". So my ideation has never been "I cannot go on, it hurts too much"; it's been "if I can't leave the country in five years, then I'm going to have to kill myself, because I'm going to lose my rights anyway". 

This is why it's become so critical for me to take a step back. I already do way more than most people would in contributing to the things that matter, but my brain has had the idea drilled into it by itself that I needed to help others at the cost of myself, like giving pieces of myself, was the thing I was obligated to do to help make the world at least a little bit better for other people. 

But doing that doesn't help me, and it won't help anyone else substantially enough to avoid diminishing returns. So I need to stop. I already donate $ 45 a month to Food Not Bombs, the Electronic Frontier Foundation, and the Control AI initiative. That's almost $500 annually to non-profits. Despite that, I still sometimes feel like I need to do more, like volunteering or writing more letters to Congress than I already have. 

That's why I need to stop. I really need to stop. I do enough that watching the news doesn't deserve my attention. It never will, and I may need to cut it off entirely, as well as other similar things. They now only ever serve to make my life more painful than it needs to be, to the point that I sometimes forget to even drink water.
